CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding - positive Lyme titer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Michelle is a 31-year-old female with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension who presents with a positive Lyme titer. She reports having an insect bite approximately two weeks ago while hiking in the woods. She is currently experiencing fatigue and lack of energy, swollen joints in her elbows with pain, body aches, nausea, and poor appetite, able to tolerate only toast and crackers. She reports noticing a bull's eye rash. She denies high fevers. Regarding her diabetes, she reports blood sugars have been okay, though occasionally running a little high or low but nothing too far out of range. She is monitoring her blood pressure at home with readings that have been good and has been staying away from salty foods.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Endorses nausea, joint pain, and body aches. Denies abdominal pain, diarrhea, and high fevers.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin
Lisinopril

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent hiking in the woods approximately two weeks ago. Avoiding salty foods.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs look great with no fever at this time. Bilateral elbow joint swelling with pain to palpation. Bull's eye rash on abdomen on the left-hand side, warm to palpation, non-tender to palpation, no evidence of cellulitis. Heart and lungs examined. Rest of exam is normal.

RESULTS
Lyme titer is elevated. Labs show everything else looks good with no elevated white blood cell count.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly diagnosed Lyme disease: Prescribe doxycycline 100 milligrams twice a day for three weeks. Consult with infectious disease doctor. Follow-up appointment next week.

2. Type 2 diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c. Continue metformin.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Order lipid panel. Continue to record blood pressure regularly. Refill lisinopril.
